metadata.title: Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning
metadata.authors: Mnih, Kavukcuoglu, Silver, Rusu, Veness, et al.
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Optimal action-value function $Q^*(s,a)$
nodes.statement: $Q^*(s,a) = \max_\pi \mathbb{E}[R_t \mid s_t = s, a_t = a, \pi]$, the maximum discounted future return achievable from state $s$ taking action $a$ under any policy $\pi$.
nodes.statement_clean: The optimal action-value is the maximum expected discounted return obtainable from state s after action a under any policy.

nodes.name: Discounted return $R_t$
nodes.statement: $R_t = \sum_{t'=t}^{T} \gamma^{t'-t} r_{t'}$, the future reward accumulated from time $t$ until episode termination $T$, discounted by factor $\gamma$ per time-step (set to $0.99$).
nodes.statement_clean: Future discounted return is the gamma-weighted sum of rewards from time t to terminal time T.

nodes.name: Q-network
nodes.statement: A neural-network function approximator $Q(s,a;\theta)$ with parameters $\theta$ that estimates the action-value function $Q^*(s,a)$.
nodes.statement_clean: A Q-network is a neural network that approximates the action-value function with parameters theta.

nodes.name: Experience replay memory $D$
nodes.statement: A dataset $D_t = \{e_1, \ldots, e_t\}$ storing the agent's transitions $e_t = (s_t, a_t, r_t, s_{t+1})$ at each time-step, from which minibatches are sampled uniformly at random during Q-learning updates. The buffer keeps the last $N$ tuples.
nodes.statement_clean: Experience replay memory is a buffer of recent transitions sampled uniformly at random for Q-learning updates.

nodes.name: Target Q-network $\hat{Q}$
nodes.statement: A separate network $\hat{Q}$ with parameters $\theta^{-}$ used to generate the Q-learning targets $y_j$. Its weights are cloned from the online network $Q$ every $C$ updates and held fixed in between.
nodes.statement_clean: The target Q-network is a periodically updated copy of the online Q-network used to compute stable training targets.

nodes.name: Preprocessing map $\phi$
nodes.statement: Function that takes the most recent $m=4$ raw Atari frames, applies pixel-wise max with the previous frame to remove flicker, extracts the Y luminance channel, rescales to $84 \times 84$, and stacks them to form an $84 \times 84 \times 4$ input to the Q-network.
nodes.statement_clean: Preprocessing reduces and stacks four recent Atari frames into an 84x84x4 luminance image input to the Q-network.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-greedy policy
nodes.statement: A behaviour policy that selects the greedy action $a = \arg\max_{a'} Q(s,a';\theta)$ with probability $1-\epsilon$ and a uniformly random action with probability $\epsilon$, used to ensure adequate exploration.
nodes.statement_clean: The epsilon-greedy policy explores with probability epsilon and exploits the greedy Q-action with probability 1-epsilon.

nodes.name: Deep Q-Network (DQN) agent
nodes.statement: An artificial agent combining Q-learning with a deep convolutional neural network, trained end-to-end from raw pixel inputs and game scores using experience replay and a periodically updated target network.
nodes.statement_clean: DQN is the deep convolutional Q-learning agent introduced by the paper that learns Atari policies from pixels.

nodes.name: DQN loss function $L_i(\theta_i)$
nodes.statement: $L_i(\theta_i) = \mathbb{E}_{(s,a,r,s') \sim U(D)} \left[ \left( r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s',a'; \theta_i^{-}) - Q(s,a; \theta_i) \right)^2 \right]$.
nodes.statement_clean: The DQN loss is the expected squared TD error between the bootstrapped target using the target network and the online Q-value, over uniformly sampled replay transitions.

nodes.name: Bellman optimality equation
nodes.statement: $Q^*(s,a) = \mathbb{E}_{s'}\left[ r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q^*(s',a') \mid s,a \right]$.
nodes.statement_clean: The optimal Q-function satisfies the Bellman equation: it equals the expected reward plus the discounted max next-state Q-value.

nodes.name: DQN gradient update
nodes.statement: $\nabla_{\theta_i} L(\theta_i) = \mathbb{E}_{s,a,r,s'} \left[ \left( r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s',a';\theta_i^{-}) - Q(s,a;\theta_i) \right) \nabla_{\theta_i} Q(s,a;\theta_i) \right]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Differentiating the DQN loss gives the TD-error-weighted gradient of the online Q-network.

nodes.name: Learning Atari control from high-dimensional sensory input
nodes.statement: Train a single agent that, using the same algorithm, network architecture, and hyperparameters, learns successful control policies for $49$ Atari 2600 games from raw pixel input ($210 \times 160$ RGB at $60$ Hz) and the game score, with no game-specific feature engineering.
nodes.statement_clean: Learn a single end-to-end RL agent that masters 49 Atari games from pixels and score using one fixed architecture and hyperparameters.

nodes.name: Instability of nonlinear Q-learning
nodes.statement: Q-learning with a nonlinear function approximator (e.g. a neural network) is known to be unstable or to diverge, due to correlations in the observation sequence, sensitivity of the policy to small Q updates, and correlations between $Q$ and the bootstrapped target $r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s',a')$.
nodes.statement_clean: Combining Q-learning with neural network function approximators is unstable due to data correlations and target coupling.

nodes.name: Deep Q-learning with experience replay (Algorithm 1)
nodes.statement: Online Q-learning with a deep convolutional Q-network, an experience replay buffer sampled uniformly for minibatch updates, and a separately-updated target network for computing Bellman targets.
nodes.statement_clean: DQN training: collect transitions into replay memory, sample minibatches, take gradient steps on the squared TD error, and periodically refresh the target network.
input: Number of episodes $M$ and per-episode horizon $T$
Exploration rate $\epsilon$ (annealed from $1.0$ to $0.1$ over the first million frames)

nodes.name: Frame-skipping
nodes.statement: The agent selects an action only on every $k$-th frame ($k=4$) and repeats the last selected action on the intervening skipped frames, allowing roughly $k$x more game time per unit of compute.
nodes.statement_clean: Frame-skipping reuses the same action for k=4 frames so the emulator advances faster between agent decisions.
output: Action stream with one decision every $k$ frames, last action repeated otherwise

nodes.name: RMSProp optimizer
nodes.statement: Stochastic gradient descent with RMSProp, run on minibatches of size $32$, used to optimize the DQN loss $L_i(\theta_i)$.
nodes.statement_clean: RMSProp is the per-parameter adaptive SGD optimizer used to train the Q-network.

nodes.name: t-SNE
nodes.statement: A nonlinear dimensionality-reduction algorithm for visualizing high-dimensional data in two dimensions, applied to the last-hidden-layer DQN representations to reveal that perceptually or value-similar Atari states are mapped to nearby points.
nodes.statement_clean: t-SNE is the visualization algorithm used to embed DQN's last-hidden-layer representations of Atari states in 2D.

nodes.name: Convolutional Q-network architecture
nodes.statement: Network mapping an $84 \times 84 \times 4$ stacked-frame input to one Q-value per legal action via three convolutional layers followed by a fully-connected layer.
nodes.statement_clean: DQN's deep CNN: three conv layers and one fully-connected layer mapping 84x84x4 frames to per-action Q-values.
output: A vector of Q-values, one per legal action ($4$ to $18$ actions per game)
nodes.pseudocode: Conv1: 32 filters of 8x8, stride 4, ReLU; Conv2: 64 filters of 4x4, stride 2, ReLU; Conv3: 64 filters of 3x3, stride 1, ReLU; FC: 512 units, ReLU; Output: linear layer with one unit per valid action.

nodes.name: Convergence of value iteration
nodes.statement: The value-iteration update $Q_{i+1}(s,a) = \mathbb{E}_{s'}[r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q_i(s',a') \mid s,a]$ converges to the optimal action-value function: $Q_i \to Q^*$ as $i \to \infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Repeated Bellman backups converge to the optimal Q-function in the tabular setting.
nodes.origin_citation: Sutton & Barto 1998 (RL textbook); classical dynamic programming

nodes.name: Human-level performance across 49 Atari games
nodes.statement: Trained with a single fixed algorithm, network, and hyperparameter set, DQN exceeds the best previously published RL methods on $43$ of $49$ Atari 2600 games and reaches at least $75\%$ of professional-human-tester score on $29$ of them.
nodes.statement_clean: DQN beats the prior RL state of the art on 43/49 Atari games and matches/exceeds 75% of human level on 29/49.

nodes.name: Replay and target-network ablation
nodes.statement: Disabling either experience replay or the separate target Q-network substantially degrades DQN performance across games, demonstrating that both mechanisms are core contributors to stability and final score.
nodes.statement_clean: Ablating replay or the target network sharply lowers DQN's scores, confirming both are necessary.

nodes.name: Deep convolutional architecture beats linear approximator
nodes.statement: Replacing the convolutional Q-network with a single linear layer (while keeping replay and target network) yields markedly worse performance on the five validation games, showing the importance of the deep representation.
nodes.statement_clean: Swapping DQN's CNN for a linear approximator severely degrades performance, confirming depth matters.

nodes.name: Reward clipping
nodes.statement: Positive rewards are clipped at $+1$, negative rewards at $-1$, leaving zero rewards unchanged. This standardizes error magnitudes across games but prevents the agent from distinguishing rewards of different magnitude.
nodes.statement_clean: Rewards are clipped to {-1, 0, +1} so a single learning rate works across all games.

nodes.name: Error clipping (Huber-like loss)
nodes.statement: The TD error $r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s',a';\theta_i^{-}) - Q(s,a;\theta_i)$ is clipped to $[-1,1]$, which corresponds to using an absolute-value (Huber-like) loss outside that interval and improves training stability.
nodes.statement_clean: Clipping the TD error to [-1,1] yields a Huber-like loss that further stabilizes training.

nodes.name: Off-policy nature of DQN
nodes.statement: DQN learns off-policy: experience-replay samples are drawn from a behaviour distribution different from the current greedy policy, which motivates the use of Q-learning rather than an on-policy update.
nodes.statement_clean: Replay-based learning is off-policy, which is precisely why Q-learning (not SARSA) is the right update.

nodes.name: Space Invaders learning curves and t-SNE embedding
nodes.statement: On Space Invaders, average score per episode and average predicted action-value rise smoothly over $200$ training epochs (Fig. 2a,c). A 2D t-SNE embedding of last-hidden-layer activations groups perceptually similar and value-similar game states together (Fig. 4).
nodes.statement_clean: Space Invaders training curves and t-SNE plots illustrate stable learning and meaningful learned representations.

nodes.name: Breakout long-term tunnel strategy
nodes.statement: On Breakout, DQN discovers the long-term strategy of digging a tunnel along the side of the wall to send the ball behind the bricks; the learned value function rises in anticipation of clearing many bricks at once.
nodes.statement_clean: DQN learns Breakout's tunnel exploit and its value function reflects the anticipated reward burst.

nodes.name: Pong learned action-values
nodes.statement: On Pong, the value of the 'up' action stays high while the 'down' action's value drops to about $-0.9$ as the ball approaches; expected reward rises to $\approx 1$ as the ball reaches the screen edge after a successful return.
nodes.statement_clean: On Pong, DQN's per-action Q-values track the consequences of pressing up vs. down at each moment.

nodes.name: Montezuma's Revenge failure mode
nodes.statement: DQN does not solve games requiring temporally extended planning over long horizons, such as Montezuma's Revenge, where its score remains far below human performance.
nodes.statement_clean: Montezuma's Revenge exemplifies long-horizon-planning games where DQN fails.

nodes.name: Derivation of the DQN gradient
nodes.statement: Differentiating the squared TD-error loss $L_i(\theta_i)$ with respect to $\theta_i$ — treating the target parameters $\theta_i^{-}$ as fixed and noting that the variance term in the equivalent decomposition does not depend on $\theta_i$ — yields the gradient of equation $\nabla_{\theta_i} L(\theta_i)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Taking partial derivatives of the squared TD-error loss with frozen target parameters gives the DQN gradient.

nodes.name: Initialize replay memory and networks
nodes.statement: Initialize replay memory $D$ to capacity $N$; initialize action-value network $Q$ with random weights $\theta$; initialize target network $\hat{Q}$ with weights $\theta^{-} = \theta$.

nodes.name: Episode loop
nodes.statement: For $\text{episode} = 1, \ldots, M$: initialize the raw sequence $s_1 = \{x_1\}$ and its preprocessing $\phi_1 = \phi(s_1)$.

nodes.name: Inner time-step loop: act $\epsilon$-greedily
nodes.statement: For $t = 1, \ldots, T$: with probability $\epsilon$ select a random action $a_t$; otherwise select $a_t = \arg\max_a Q(\phi(s_t), a; \theta)$.

nodes.name: Execute action and store transition
nodes.statement: Execute $a_t$ in the emulator, observe reward $r_t$ and image $x_{t+1}$; set $s_{t+1} = s_t, a_t, x_{t+1}$ and $\phi_{t+1} = \phi(s_{t+1})$; store transition $(\phi_t, a_t, r_t, \phi_{t+1})$ in $D$.

nodes.name: Sample minibatch and form target $y_j$
nodes.statement: Sample a random minibatch of transitions $(\phi_j, a_j, r_j, \phi_{j+1})$ from $D$. Set $y_j = r_j$ if the episode terminates at step $j+1$, else $y_j = r_j + \gamma \max_{a'} \hat{Q}(\phi_{j+1}, a'; \theta^{-})$.

nodes.name: Gradient descent on TD error
nodes.statement: Perform a gradient-descent step on $\left( y_j - Q(\phi_j, a_j; \theta) \right)^2$ with respect to the network parameters $\theta$ (using RMSProp).

nodes.name: Periodically refresh target network
nodes.statement: Every $C$ steps, reset $\hat{Q} = Q$ (clone the online network's weights into the target network).
